So, let's say for a second that there is this pill. Everyone can get as many of them as they want, but two people must take it together. Every single time you take it, you feel amazing for a few minutes. And 99.9% of the time there are absolutely no negative side effects.

Nobody has to take them, but a lot of people do.

Like I said, 99.9% of the time, there is absolutely no downside to taking the pill. But 0.1% of the time, both of the people who took the pill together will have an adverse reaction. The reaction is almost never fatal.

One of the partners will experience no physical pain, but the pill will cause variable amounts of emotional instability for the rest of their lives. The other 50% experiences 9 months of physical discomfort, followed by a fairly severe amount of pain, in addition to a similar amount of emotional instability as their partner. In either case, the financial cost of the side effect is typically tends to be in the hundreds of thousands of dollars, but can actually be much higher than that.

Everyone who took the pill was informed of the potential side effects. Nobody forced or coerced them.

Now, here is the important part. Once you've taken the pill, there is absolutely no possible way to change your mind.

Should you feel sorry for the people who take the pill, and then later say that they regret it?

Do your feelings change based on whether they are physically discomforted, or only emotionally or financially?
When people are informed and know the risks; it's their choice. no remorse.
